title: Chapter 32. Nagari Padas — VI: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 146–168): the townswomen's daydreams and the talk of the heavenly women
html:
On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.

1. Narahari — "śuna śuna badhū eta dine bidhi…" (GPT1 pp. 221–222, no. 146; GCC 9.2)

Nagari-bhava (a mother-in-law's speech). An elderly woman tells her daughters-in-law: yesterday an astrologer came to their house who knows what is in everyone's mind; when she asked how good fortune might come, he told her to honour Shachi-devi, Nimaichand's mother: the dust of her feet removes the threefold miseries, whoever sees her face at dawn knows no sorrow, and whoever reviles her is destroyed by the goddess Ugrachanda; so every morning she should send her daughters-in-law to her house. The mother-in-law hurries the young wives off to Shachi — and they, covering their faces, make a show of pleading their household work. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 9, pada 2.1

শুন শুন বধূ এত দিনে বিধি প্রসন্ন হইল মোরে ।
গত দিন দিন-প্রহর সময়ে দৈবজ্ঞ আইল ঘরে ॥

śuna śuna badhū eta dine bidhi prasanna haila more |
gata dina dina-prahara samaye daibajña āila ghare ||

śuna śuna badhū — listen, listen, daughters-in-law; eta dine — at last (lit. "after so many days"); bidhi prasanna haila more — the Creator has become gracious to me; gata dina — yesterday; dina-prahara samaye — at the time of the day-watch (prahara — a "watch" of the day); daibajña āila ghare — an astrologer came to the house

1.1"Listen, listen, daughters-in-law: at last the Creator has become gracious to me! Yesterday, at the time of the day-watch, an astrologer came to our house.

কি কহিব তার গুণগণ মেন এমন না দেখি এথা ।
যেবা যা পুছয়ে তাহা কহে সব জানয়ে মনের কথা ॥

ki kahiba tāra guṇagaṇa mena emana nā dekhi ethā |
yebā yā puchaye tāhā kahe saba jānaye manera kathā ||

ki kahiba — what shall I say; tāra guṇagaṇa — of his virtues; mena (= yena) — as it were; emana nā dekhi ethā — such a one I have not seen here; yebā yā puchaye — whatever anyone asks; tāhā kahe saba — he tells it all; jānaye manera kathā — he knows what is in the mind

1.2What shall I say of his virtues — such a one, truly, I have never seen here: whatever anyone asks, he tells it all — he knows what is in a person's mind.

কিরূপে মঙ্গল হবে বলি মুই ধরিনু তাহার পা ।
আমারে আতুর দেখি কহে কিছু চিন্তা না করিহ মা ॥

kirūpe maṅgala habe bali mui dharinu tāhāra pā |
āmāre ātura dekhi kahe kichu cintā nā kariha mā ||

kirūpe maṅgala habe — how will good come; bali — saying; mui dharinu tāhāra pā — I clasped his feet; āmāre ātura dekhi — seeing me anxious; kahe — he says; kichu cintā nā kariha — do not worry at all; mā — mother

1.3'How will good fortune come?' I said, and clasped his feet. Seeing my anxiety, he says: 'Do not worry at all, mother.

তোমাদের গ্রামে শচীদেবী বৈসে না জান মহিমা তাঁর ।
পরম পূজিতা জগতের মাঝে বিদিত চরিত যাঁর ॥

tomādera grāme śacīdebī baise nā jāna mahimā tām̐ra |
parama pūjitā jagatera mājhe bidita carita yām̐ra ||

tomādera grāme — in your village; śacīdebī baise — lives Shachi-devi; nā jāna mahimā tām̐ra — do you not know her greatness; parama pūjitā — supremely honoured; jagatera mājhe — in the world; bidita carita yām̐ra — whose deeds are renowned

1.4In your village lives Shachi-devi — do you not know her greatness? She is supremely honoured in the world; her deeds are known to all.

অতি সুলভ তাঁর পদরজ যে জন ধরএ শিরে ।
ধনজন হবে এ কি বড় কথা তুরিতে ত্রিতাপ হরে ॥

ati sulabha tām̐ra padaraja ye jana dharae śire |
dhanajana habe e ki baṛa kathā turite tritāpa hare ||

ati sulabha — very easily had; tām̐ra padaraja — the dust of her feet; ye jana dharae śire — whoever places on the head; dhanajana habe — wealth and kin will come; e ki baṛa kathā — is that anything great; turite — swiftly; tritāpa hare — it removes the threefold miseries

1.5Very easily had is the dust of her feet: whoever places it on his head will have wealth and kin — but what is great in that! — at once it removes the threefold miseries.

রজনীপ্রভাতে উঠিয়া যে জন দেখয়ে তাঁহার মুখ ।
জনমে জনমে সে সুখে ভাসয়ে কভু না জানয়ে দুখ ॥

rajanīprabhāte uṭhiyā ye jana dekhaye tām̐hāra mukha |
janame janame se sukhe bhāsaye kabhu nā jānaye dukha ||

rajanīprabhāte uṭhiyā — rising at dawn; ye jana dekhaye tām̐hāra mukha — whoever sees her face; janame janame — birth after birth; se sukhe bhāsaye — floats in happiness; kabhu nā jānaye dukha — never knows sorrow

1.6Whoever rises at dawn and sees her face floats in happiness birth after birth and never knows sorrow.

শচীমায়ে যেবা নিন্দয়ে সে দুখ-আনলে পুড়িয়া মরে ।
নিশ্চয় জানিহ উগ্রচণ্ডা দেবী তাহারে সংহার করে ॥

śacīmāye yebā nindaye se dukha-ānale puṛiyā mare |
niścaya jāniha ugracaṇḍā debī tāhāre saṃhāra kare ||

śacīmāye yebā nindaye — whoever reviles Mother Shachi; se — he; dukha-ānale puṛiyā mare — burns to death in the fire of sorrow; niścaya jāniha — know for certain; ugracaṇḍā debī — the goddess Ugrachanda; tāhāre saṃhāra kare — destroys him

1.7Whoever reviles Mother Shachi burns to death in the fire of sorrow; know for certain: the goddess Ugrachanda destroys him.

তাহে উপদেশ দিয়া বধূগণে মনের কপট ছাড়ি ।
নিশি পরভাতে যতনে পাঠাবে শ্রীশচীদেবীর বাড়ী ॥

tāhe upadeśa diyā badhūgaṇe manera kapaṭa chāṛi |
niśi parabhāte yatane pāṭhābe śrīśacīdebīra bāṛī ||

tāhe — therefore; upadeśa diyā badhūgaṇe — instructing your daughters-in-law; manera kapaṭa chāṛi — giving up all guile of heart; niśi parabhāte — at the break of night; yatane pāṭhābe — send them with care; śrī-śacīdebīra bāṛī — to the house of Sri Shachi-devi

1.8Therefore, instructing your daughters-in-law and giving up all guile of heart, send them with care at daybreak to the house of Sri Shachi-devi.

তেঁহ কৃপা করি করিবে আশীষ পূরিবে মনের আশ ।
বাড়িবে সম্পদ সদা সুখ বহু বিপদ হইবে নাশ ॥

tem̐ha kṛpā kari karibe āśīṣa pūribe manera āśa |
bāṛibe sampada sadā sukha bahu bipada haibe nāśa ||

tem̐ha kṛpā kari — she, being gracious; karibe āśīṣa — will bless; pūribe manera āśa — the heart's wish will be fulfilled; bāṛibe sampada — prosperity will grow; sadā sukha bahu — always much happiness; bipada haibe nāśa — misfortunes will be destroyed

1.9She will be gracious and bless them — and the heart's wish will be fulfilled: prosperity will grow, there will always be much happiness, misfortunes will be destroyed.

পরদুঃখে দুঃখী নিতান্ত জানিহ নিমাইচাঁদের মায় ।
এইরূপ কত কহি অন্য বাড়ী গেলেন দৈবজ্ঞরায় ॥

paraduḥkhe duḥkhī nitānta jāniha nimāicām̐dera māya |
eirūpa kata kahi anya bāṛī gelena daibajñarāya ||

paraduḥkhe duḥkhī — grieved by others' grief; nitānta jāniha — know for sure; nimāicām̐dera māya — Nimaichand's mother; eirūpa kata kahi — saying much like this; anya bāṛī gelena — went on to another house; daibajñarāya — the worthy astrologer

1.10Know for sure: Nimaichand's mother grieves at others' grief.' Saying much like this, the worthy astrologer went on to another house.2

এ সকল কথা শুনিয়া আমার বড়ই আনন্দ হৈল ।
মনে অনুভব কৈনু হেন যেন সব অমঙ্গল গেল ॥

e sakala kathā śuniyā āmāra baṛai ānanda haila |
mane anubhaba kainu hena yena saba amaṅgala gela ||

e sakala kathā śuniyā — hearing all this; āmāra baṛai ānanda haila — I became very glad; mane anubhaba kainu — I felt in my heart; hena yena — as if; saba amaṅgala gela — all ill fortune had gone

1.11Hearing all this I was very glad: I felt in my heart as if all ill fortune had gone.

তাহাতে তোমরা যাও শীঘ্র করি সে হয় আমার ঘর ।
দিদি বলি মোরে আদর করে সে কভু না জানয়ে পর ॥

tāhāte tomarā yāo śīghra kari se haya āmāra ghara |
didi bali more ādara kare se kabhu nā jānaye para ||

tāhāte — so; tomarā yāo śīghra kari — go quickly; se haya āmāra ghara — she is my own (lit. "she is my house"); didi bali — calling me "elder sister"; more ādara kare — treats me fondly; se kabhu nā jānaye para — she never regards anyone as a stranger

1.12So go quickly: she is my own — she calls me 'elder sister', treats me fondly, and never regards anyone as a stranger.

তথা গিয়া তাঁরে প্রণাম করিয়া কহিয়ে বিনয়-বাণী ।
তাঁহার কৃপায় হবে সব সুখ ইহা ত নিশ্চয় জানি ॥

tathā giyā tām̐re praṇāma kariyā kahiye binaya-bāṇī |
tām̐hāra kṛpāya habe saba sukha ihā ta niścaya jāni ||

tathā giyā — going there; tām̐re praṇāma kariyā — bowing to her; kahiye binaya-bāṇī — speak humble words; tām̐hāra kṛpāya — by her grace; habe saba sukha — all happiness will come; ihā ta niścaya jāni — this I know for certain

1.13When you get there, bow to her and speak humble words: by her grace all happiness will come — this I know for certain.

তোমা সবা প্রতি তেঁহ কহিবেন এ বেলা থাকহ এথা ।
তাহে কোন ছলে আসিবে সকালে আমি যে যাইব সেথা ॥

tomā sabā prati tem̐ha kahibena e belā thākaha ethā |
tāhe kona chale āsibe sakāle āmi ye yāiba sethā ||

tomā sabā prati — to you all; tem̐ha kahibena — she will say; e belā thākaha ethā — stay here this morning; tāhe — then; kona chale — on some pretext; āsibe sakāle — come back early; āmi ye yāiba sethā — for I myself shall go there

1.14She will say to you all: 'Stay here this morning,' — then come back early on some pretext: for I myself shall be going there."

শাশুড়ীর অতি আতুর বচন শুনিয়া অধিক সুখে ।
আদর লাগিয়া ধীরে ধীরে কহে বসন ঝাঁপিয়া মুখে ॥

śāśuṛīra ati ātura bacana śuniyā adhika sukhe |
ādara lāgiyā dhīre dhīre kahe basana jhām̐piyā mukhe ||

śāśuṛīra ati ātura bacana — the mother-in-law's most eager words; śuniyā adhika sukhe — hearing with great joy; ādara lāgiyā — to be coaxed; dhīre dhīre kahe — [one] says softly; basana jhām̐piyā mukhe — covering her face with her cloth

1.15Hearing the mother-in-law's most eager words, [the young wives] are overjoyed; and, to be coaxed a little more, one says very softly, covering her face with her cloth:

প্রভাত সময়ে কেমনে ছাড়িয়া যাইব ঘরের কাজ ।
নরহরি কহে আসিয়া করিবা এখন না সহে ব্যাজ ॥

prabhāta samaye kemane chāṛiyā yāiba gharera kāja |
narahari kahe āsiyā karibā ekhana nā sahe byāja ||

prabhāta samaye — at the time of dawn; kemane chāṛiyā yāiba — how can we go, leaving; gharera kāja — the household work; narahari kahe — Narahari says; āsiyā kariba — you will come back and do it; ekhana nā sahe byāja — now there must be no delay

1.16"How can we go in the morning, leaving the household work?" Narahari says: "You will come back and do it; now there must be no delay."3

pp. 106–107; scan PDF pp. 111–112), "bṛddhāha — yathārāga" ("the old woman said"). The ninth kirana of GCC ("Again in the morning — the outings of the nagaris of Navadvipa, their wishes, their darshan and so on"; it opens with GCC 9.1, no. 23 of chapter 31) tells how the mothers-in-law themselves send their daughters-in-law to Shachi-devi; GPT omits GCC 9.3–9.5 — the mother-in-law coaxes the young wives again, they dress, bow to her and set out (9.3), the joyful procession of the young women (9.4, Vrajabuli, raga lalita) and the first of their "wishes" — to bow to Shachi and steal a glance at Gauranga (9.5). Before 9.5 the author has a Sanskrit rubric, "their wishes (manoratha) he relates in order": the following padas (nos. 2–12 of this chapter) are these wishes. GCC readings: "parama ānanda" (1.11), "yāha śīghra kari" (1.12), "āsiyā karibe" (1.16). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). Lord, worthy of the whole world's reverence). The "threefold miseries" (tritāpa) — those caused by one's own body and mind, by other beings and by the forces of nature. Ugrachanda (ugracaṇḍā) is a fierce form of Durga (Chandi); the threat to those who revile Shachi is the village astrologer's word, rendered as in the original. The promise "will have wealth and kin — but what is great in that" (1.5) the poet puts in the astrologer's mouth so that the mother-in-law, mindful of prosperity, will gladly let the young wives go (cf. the end of no. 23 of chapter 31: "there is nothing in the world but the craving for wealth"). The last line can be understood either as the mother-in-law's answer or as the poet's own word ("Narahari says…"); it is left as in the original.

2. Narahari — "sakhīsaha sukhe śrīśacīdebīra…" (GPT1 p. 222, no. 147; GCC 9.6)

Nagari-bhava; a daydream. On the way to Shachi's house a townswoman dreams: she will stand with her friend in Shachi-devi's courtyard and steal a glance at Gaura; He will answer with a sly look — and she will have neither composure nor dharma left, she will tremble at Madana's arrow and strain to embrace Gaurangachand, but her friend will hold her back by the end of her sari; the others will laugh, she will be abashed and turn away, covering her face — and Gaura will smile. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 9, pada 6.4

সখীসহ সুখে শ্রীশচীদেবীর অঙ্গনে দাঁড়াব গিয়া ।
অলখিতে তাঁরে বারেক নিরখি জুড়াব নয়ন হিয়া ॥

sakhīsaha sukhe śrīśacīdebīra aṅgane dām̐ṛāba giyā |
alakhite tām̐re bāreka nirakhi juṛāba nayana hiyā ||

sakhīsaha sukhe — gladly, with my friend; śrī-śacīdebīra aṅgane — in the courtyard of Sri Shachi-devi; dām̐ṛāba giyā — I shall go and stand; alakhite — unnoticed; tām̐re bāreka nirakhi — glancing at Him once; juṛāba nayana hiyā — I shall cool my eyes and heart

2.1"Gladly, with my friend, I shall go and stand in the courtyard of Sri Shachi-devi; unnoticed, I shall glance at Him once — and cool my eyes and heart.

সে পুনঃ মো পানে চাহিবে তাহার বিষম আঁখির ঠারে ।
ধৈরজ ধরম কিছু না থাকিবে কাঁপিব মদনশরে ॥

se punaḥ mo pāne cāhibe tāhāra biṣama ām̐khira ṭhāre |
dhairaja dharama kichu nā thākibe kām̐piba madanaśare ||

se punaḥ — He in turn; mo pāne cāhibe — will look at me; tāhāra biṣama ām̐khira ṭhāre — with the sly signal of His eyes; dhairaja dharama — composure and dharma; kichu nā thākibe — nothing will remain; kām̐piba madanaśare — I shall tremble at Madana's arrow

2.2He in turn will look at me — with the sly signal of His eyes; I shall have neither composure nor dharma left — I shall tremble at Madana's arrow.

ঘামেতে তিতিবে তনু ঘন ঘন আউলাবে মাথার কেশ ।
খসিবে বসন বারে বারে আর না রবে লাজের লেশ ॥

ghāmete titibe tanu ghana ghana āulābe māthāra keśa |
khasibe basana bāre bāre āra nā rabe lājera leśa ||

ghāmete titibe tanu — my body will be wet with sweat; ghana ghana — again and again; āulābe māthāra keśa — my hair will come loose; khasibe basana bāre bāre — my cloth will slip again and again; āra nā rabe lājera leśa — not a trace of shame will remain

2.3My body will be wet with sweat, my hair will keep coming loose; my cloth will slip again and again — not a trace of shame will remain.

গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদেরে আলিঙ্গন দিতে অধিক উদ্যত হব ।
আঁচরে ধরিয়া রাখিবেক সখী তাহার কথায় রব ॥

gaurāṅgacām̐dere āliṅgana dite adhika udyata haba |
ām̐care dhariyā rākhibeka sakhī tāhāra kathāya raba ||

gaurāṅgacām̐dere — Gaurangachand; āliṅgana dite — to embrace; adhika udyata haba — I shall be all too eager; ām̐care dhariyā — seizing the end of my sari; rākhibeka sakhī — my friend will hold me back; tāhāra kathāya raba — I shall heed her word

2.4I shall be all too eager to embrace Gaurangachand — my friend will hold me back by the end of my sari; I shall heed her word.

মোরে এইরূপ হেরি আনে আনে করিব কতেক হাসি ।
সে সব বুঝিয়া থির হব চিতে কিঞ্চিৎ সঙ্কোচ বাসি ॥

more eirūpa heri āne āne kariba kateka hāsi |
se saba bujhiyā thira haba cite kiñcit saṅkoca bāsi ||

more eirūpa heri — seeing me so; āne āne — the others among themselves; kariba kateka hāsi — will laugh a good deal; se saba bujhiyā — understanding all that; thira haba cite — I shall grow calm at heart; kiñcit saṅkoca bāsi — feeling a little abashed

2.5Seeing me so, the others will laugh a good deal among themselves; understanding all that, I shall grow calm at heart, a little abashed.

বিমুখী হইয়া দাঁড়াইব পুনঃ বসন ঝাঁপিয়া মুখে ।
নরহরি-প্রাণনাথে তাহা দেখি হাসিবে মনের সুখে ॥

bimukhī haiyā dām̐ṛāiba punaḥ basana jhām̐piyā mukhe |
narahari-prāṇanāthe tāhā dekhi hāsibe manera sukhe ||

bimukhī haiyā — turning away; dām̐ṛāiba punaḥ — I shall stand again; basana jhām̐piyā mukhe — covering my face with my cloth; narahari-prāṇanāthe — the Lord of Narahari's life; tāhā dekhi — seeing this; hāsibe manera sukhe — will smile with joy of heart

2.6Turning away, I shall stand again, covering my face with my cloth; the Lord of Narahari's life, seeing this, will smile with joy of heart."5

This is the second of the "wishes" (manoratha) of the townswomen on their way to Shachi's house (note 1): all the padas nos. 2–12 are in the future tense ("I shall stand", "I shall glance", "He will say"), i.e. not an account of what happened but what each one pictures to herself on the way. Summary of chapter 32

The chapter continues the padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT. All 23 padas have been found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani" and checked against its scan ("probably Chakravarti" — B). No. 146 (no. 1) = GCC 9.2 — a mother-in-law, on an astrologer's word, sends her daughters-in-law to Shachi-devi. Nos. 147–157 (nos. 2–12) = GCC 9.6–9.16 — the "wishes" (manoratha) of the townswomen on the way to Shachi's house, all in the future tense: to steal a glance at Gaura, feigned mana, a silent conversation of the eyes, reproaches; in GCC no. 150 comes after no. 153 (9.12). Nos. 158–168 (nos. 13–23) = GCC 10.10–10.24 — according to GCC this is the conversation and dispute of heavenly women (debaramaṇī) looking down on Nadia from the sky: some speak of the "secret play of the nagara", others (nos. 19–20) answer with a description of the Lord's strictness — He does not look at women, does not listen to talk of them, bathes in a secluded place — and call slander of Him an aparadha; the dispute ends with mockery and the argument "Shachi's son is Yashoda's son, a nature cannot be given up" (nos. 21–23). Section 3.2 of GPT omits GCC 9.3–9.5, 9.17–9.23, 10.1–10.9, 10.11, 10.18, 10.20, 10.23 (some of them — 9.18–9.19, 9.21–9.22, 10.7–10.9 — stand in other sections of GPT, see the concluding note of chapter 33). Where GCC is more explicit than GPT (no. 9 — "the cloth over the breast" instead of "the cloth over the face"; no. 10 — "wants to embrace" instead of "wants to see your dear face"; no. 2 — "under Madana's weight"), the GPT text is translated and the GCC reading is noted in VAR and in a note. The motifs of attraction in the townswomen's daydreams and the talk of the "nagara" are rendered exactly, without softening, with notes on the position of the tradition (notes 5, 25, 27, 30, 41, 43).
